expression_comparison.chosen_because: The discrepancy lives in cyclical FX pricing, not in a 5y-extreme curve or in already-99th-percentile UST yields. Rates were compared first: short duration is late versus the post-hike bond rally and does not own NZD cheapness; 2s10s is only extreme on a 1y window; CA-US/AU-US RV either encodes a Canada energy-hawk story or an Australia housing story, and NZ yields are missing. Spot NZDUSD is the instrument that actually jointly owns underappreciated global/US-cycle resilience, excessive defensive USD pricing after a known hike, and a live NZ growth catalyst, without forcing a vol overlay.

considered_rates.assessment: US 5Y 4.78 and 10Y 4.94 sit at the 98th–99th 1y and 99th 5y percentiles, with 5Y +41bp and 10Y +23bp over 1m, which is the growth-plus-inflation higher-for-longer tape. Short duration would own resilient nominal growth, but yields are already historically high, both tenors rallied 7–8bp on 2026-09-17 after a fully priced hike, and duration does not harvest the NZD 5y-cheap / post-FOMC USD squeeze that is the actual risk-appetite discrepancy. Rejected as the cleaner expression.

US 2s10s is 27bp, 1y 1.4th percentile, −25bp over 1m, which looks like a growth-scare flatten. A steepener is the textbook no-recession rates expression, but the 5y percentile is only 56th (z_5y +0.37), so the stretch is one-year change not a 5y broken-cycle level. Steepening also mixes bull and bear paths and leaves the FX defensive premium unowned. Rejected.

CA-US 2Y is −139bp, 4.8th 1y and 4.7th 5y percentile as of 2026-09-16: Canada is the extreme cheap rates RV versus the US. Paying CA versus US would express energy pass-through/BoC catch-up, not global risk-on, and CA labor 38 plus core inflation near 2% can justify the discount. AU-US 2Y is +40.5bp as of 2026-09-09 (AU source age 8 days), 89th 5y percentile, so Australia is already yield-rich versus the US while housing is contracting; fading that spread is a housing/tightening trade, not a pro-cyclical one. NZ official yields are unavailable (RBNZ B2 HTTP 403), so AU-NZ and NZ-US RV cannot be formed. Rejected.

considered_spot.assessment: NZDUSD is the only G10 USD-cross that is cheap on both 1y (21st percentile) and 5y (11th percentile) after a 1m −2.33% / 5d −1.42% dump, and it has a dated positive growth catalyst (India trade deal). AUDUSD is 75th/84th percentile and fights a verified housing-tightening channel, so it is not the under-discounted cyclical. Short AUDNZD (spot 1.2388, 99.96th 5y percentile, z_5y +2.96) is the tighter statistical RV and maps AU housing versus NZ trade news, but in a true risk-on/global-growth upswing AUD usually has higher beta, so fading AUDNZD can lose the optimistic regime even if both rise. NZDJPY (−4.41% 1m, 22nd 1y percentile) has more funding-currency torque, but its 5y percentile is 66th, so it is a 1m JPY-bid fade rather than a 5y cheap cyclical. Long NZDUSD owns the 5y cheapness and the post-FOMC USD event premium together.

trade.thesis: The causal gap is global risk appetite and US-cycle resilience versus a post-FOMC USD squeeze into the cheapest G10 cyclical. US retained gauges remain warm (activity 69, labor 75, consumer 74, inflation 72) after a 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% that futures had already assigned >90% odds. NZDUSD’s ECB-reference cross is 0.5743, 21st percentile 1y and 11th percentile 5y, down 2.33% 1m and 1.42% 5d, while parliament just passed an India deal cutting tariffs on about 95% of NZ exports. That is change plus a live growth transmission, not a stale level. AUD is the wrong cyclical: housing is already transmitting (NSW stamp duty −24% y/y, volumes −18%, Sydney/Melbourne values >7% off peak) and AUDUSD is 75th/84th percentile with AUDNZD at the 99.96th 5y percentile. Short duration or a 2s10s steepener can be consistent with no-recession, but they do not own the FX defensive premium that actually moved.
why_now: September 16 FOMC 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% was >90% priced into the decision, so the residual 5d USD bid is the incremental mispricing.
Saudi ship-to-ship crude via Oman reduced the extreme oil-supply tail and oil eased modestly, easing a global risk-off transmission.
NZ India-trade legislation is a dated growth catalyst while NZDUSD printed a fresh 5d/1m underperformance at a 5y-cheap percentile.
US 2Y/5Y/10Y all fell about 7–8bp on 2026-09-17 after the hike, showing the rates market is not confirming a new growth-break; cyclicals vs USD have not mean-reverted with that signal.

what_changes_my_mind: US activity/labor gauges breaking lower from 69/75 would collapse the resilient-cycle premise.
A second confirmed energy-supply shock that reverses the Oman workaround would restore the risk-off oil tail.
NZDUSD making a new 5y-cheap extreme without any India-trade or risk-appetite follow-through would say the cheapness is structural, not a squeeze.
If official NZ yields later show a large negative carry versus UST 2Y 4.67% and no closing mechanism, holding-cost would kill the tactical long.
why_now: The hike is now realized, not pending, while the 5d USD bid versus NZD is still in the tape.
NZ trade legislation and the oil-workaround headlines are dated to 2026-09-16, inside the same window as the FOMC.
US yields backing off 7–8bp on 2026-09-17 after the hike is a same-week signal that the rates market is not pricing a growth break; cyclicals have not yet closed that gap.
